How to Read a Course Description

Course numbering at the college follows one system across every department, and this page explains it so the listings that follow can be read without further help. The first part of the entry names the subject, and the part after it places the course in a level. Entries that carry a letter at the end belong to a sequence that is taken in order.

Every entry is printed in the same order, and the office that maintains this catalog keeps that order the same from one edition to the next so a reader who has learned it once does not have to learn it again.

An entry printed as ENGL 101

This description is published by the college for the current catalog and is reviewed each year by the academic department that offers it. Students should speak with an advisor before registering, since availability varies by term and by campus. The wording below is used for the print edition and the web edition alike, so the two stay identical. Questions about the text itself should go to the office that maintains the catalog rather than to the department.
